questions.problem:
Consider the polynomials ${p}_{1}(t)$ and ${p}_{2}(t),$ given by

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=2t+{t}^{3},\,{p}_{2}(t)=3-t-3{t}^{3}.
$$

Find $p(t)$ given that $B={{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}},$ and the coordinates of $p(t)$ relative to $B$ are $[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
Any vector in  $\text{Span}{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}}$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}p(t) & =2\cdot (2t+{t}^{3})+2\cdot (3-t-3{t}^{3}) \\  & =4t+2{t}^{3}+6-2t-6{t}^{3} \\  & =6+2t-4{t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=1+t+{t}^{2},\,{p}_{2}(t)=1+t-{t}^{2}.
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Any vector in  $\text{Span}{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}}$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}p(t) & =(-1)\cdot (1+t+{t}^{2})+1\cdot (1+t-{t}^{2}) \\  & =-1-t-{t}^{2}+1+t-{t}^{2} \\  & =-2{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
{B}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}],\,{B}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

If $B={{B}_{1},{B}_{2}}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}},$ and $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{B}_{1}+{x}_{2}{B}_{2}=A.
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2} & -{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} & 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=-2 \\ -{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=5 \\ 3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & -2 \\ -1 & 3 & 5 \\ 3 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & -2 \\ -1 & 3 & 5 \\ 3 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{3}{4}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & -2 \\ 0 & \frac{9}{2} & \frac{9}{2} \\ 0 & -\frac{5}{2} & -\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=-2 \\ \frac{9}{2}{x}_{2}=\frac{9}{2} \\ -\frac{5}{2}{x}_{2}=-\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second and third equations, we get ${x}_{2}=1.$ From the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+6\cdot 1 & =-2 \\ 4{x}_{1} & =-8 \\ {x}_{1} & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-2+1=-1.$

$$
{B}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}],\,{B}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}5 & -3 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -3 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

If $B={{B}_{1},{B}_{2}}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}},$ and $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{B}_{1}+{x}_{2}{B}_{2}=A.
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}5 & -3 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -3 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} & -3{x}_{2} \\ 0 & -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -3 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=4 \\ -3{x}_{2}=-3 \\ -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=5.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 4 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 \\ -2 & 4 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 4 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 \\ -2 & 4 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 4 \\ 0 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & 9 & 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=4 \\ -3{x}_{2}=-3 \\ 9{x}_{2}=9.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second and third equations, we get ${x}_{2}=1.$ From the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+5\cdot 1 & =4 \\ 2{x}_{1} & =-1 \\ {x}_{1} & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2} \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-\frac{1}{2}+1=\frac{1}{2}.$

If $B={{B}_{1},{B}_{2}}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}},$ and $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} & -3{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-4{x}_{2} & 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=1 \\ -3{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ -3 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}].

$$

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=1 \\ 9{x}_{2}=3 \\ -6{x}_{2}=-2.\end{aligned}

From the second and third equations, we get ${x}_{2}=\frac{1}{3}.$ From the first equation, we get 

$$

Therefore, $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem:
Consider the following polynomials:

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=2+{t}^{2},\,{p}_{2}(t)=1-t+2{t}^{2},\,q(t)=6+2t.
$$

If $B={{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)},$ and $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t)=q(t)
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(2+{t}^{2})+{x}_{2}(1-t+2{t}^{2}) & =6+2t \\ (2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2})-{x}_{2}t+({x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}){t}^{2} & =6+2t.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=6 \\ -{x}_{2}=2 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & \frac{3}{2} & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=6 \\ {x}_{2}=-2 \\ \frac{3}{2}{x}_{2}=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second and third equations we get ${x}_{2}=-2.$  Substituting this into the first equation yields

$$
2{x}_{1}+(-2)=6\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=4.
$$

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=4+(-2)=2.$

questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t)+{x}_{3}{p}_{3}(t)=q(t).
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(-{t}^{3}+{t}^{2}+t)+{x}_{2}(2{t}^{2}+4)+{x}_{3}(3{t}^{3}-{t}^{2}-3t+3) & =-1 \\ (-{x}_{1}+3{x}_{3}){t}^{3}+({x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}){t}^{2}+({x}_{1}-3{x}_{3})t+(4{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}) & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{1}-3{x}_{3}=0 \\ 4{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{4}+(-2){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}↔{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=0 \\ -{x}_{3}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$
